from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Configuration
        TITLE = "The Foundation: Bernoulli Trials"
        LINES = [
            "Bernoulli trials are the building blocks of binomial distributions.",
            "Meet Finn. Every fly catch is a single trial.",
            "Success means he catches the fly.",
            "Failure means the fly escapes.",
            "Finn's success rate stays constant at seventy percent."
        ]
        FINN_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        FLY_COLOR = "#A9A9A9"
        SUCCESS_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        FAILURE_COLOR = "#A9A9A9"
        TEXT_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        self.setup_layout(TITLE, LINES)
        
        # Initially hide elements to control entrance timing
        self.remove(self.title, self.lecture)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # [self.wait(2.0)] Fade in title 'Bernoulli Trial: Success or Failure' in #FFFFFF.
        self.wait(2.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title), FadeIn(self.lecture))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(SUCCESS_COLOR))
        self.wait(2.0) # L010: absorption time

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Meet Finn. Every fly catch is a single trial.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(TEXT_COLOR),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(FINN_COLOR)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)
        
        # Finn the Frog (Hand-built primitive)
        finn_body = Ellipse(width=1.2, height=0.8, color=FINN_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        eye_l = Dot(color="#000000").shift(UP*0.2 + LEFT*0.3)
        eye_r = Dot(color="#000000").shift(UP*0.2 + RIGHT*0.3)
        finn = VGroup(finn_body, eye_l, eye_r)
        self.place_at_grid(finn, "D2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # The Fly (Hand-built primitive)
        fly_body = Dot(radius=0.1, color="#333333")
        wing_l = Ellipse(width=0.2, height=0.1, color="#888888", fill_opacity=0.5).shift(LEFT*0.1 + UP*0.05)
        wing_r = Ellipse(width=0.2, height=0.1, color="#888888", fill_opacity=0.5).shift(RIGHT*0.1 + UP*0.05)
        fly = VGroup(fly_body, wing_l, wing_r)
        self.place_at_grid(fly, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(FadeIn(finn), FadeIn(fly))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Success means he catches the fly.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(TEXT_COLOR),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(SUCCESS_COLOR)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)
        
        success_label = Text("SUCCESS", color=SUCCESS_COLOR, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(success_label, "A5", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Catch animation: Tongue shoots out and retracts with fly
        tongue = Line(finn.get_top(), fly.get_center(), color="#FF69B4", stroke_width=4)
        self.play(Create(tongue), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(fly.animate.move_to(finn.get_top()), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(FadeOut(tongue), FadeOut(fly), Write(success_label))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Failure means the fly escapes.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(TEXT_COLOR),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(FAILURE_COLOR)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)
        
        # New Fly instance for the second trial
        fly_body_2 = Dot(radius=0.1, color="#333333")
        wing_l_2 = Ellipse(width=0.2, height=0.1, color="#888888", fill_opacity=0.5).shift(LEFT*0.1 + UP*0.05)
        wing_r_2 = Ellipse(width=0.2, height=0.1, color="#888888", fill_opacity=0.5).shift(RIGHT*0.1 + UP*0.05)
        fly_2 = VGroup(fly_body_2, wing_l_2, wing_r_2)
        self.place_at_grid(fly_2, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        failure_label = Text("FAILURE", color=FAILURE_COLOR, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(failure_label, "B6", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(FadeOut(success_label), FadeIn(fly_2))
        
        # Escape animation: Fly moves quickly away
        self.play(fly_2.animate.move_to(self.grid["A6"]), run_time=1)
        self.play(Write(failure_label))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Finn's success rate stays constant at seventy percent.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(TEXT_COLOR),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(SUCCESS_COLOR)
        )
        self.wait(2.0)
        
        prob_text = MathTex("p = 0.70", color=SUCCESS_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(prob_text, "D5", scale_factor=1.2)
        rect = SurroundingRectangle(prob_text, color=SUCCESS_COLOR, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Write(prob_text))
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.play(Indicate(prob_text, color=SUCCESS_COLOR)) # L004: Indicate
        self.wait(2.0)

class Section3Scene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Background and Title setup
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color="#FFFFFF").to_edge(UP)

        # Left-side lecture content logic
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color="#FFFFFF") for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define 6x6 grid system for visual placement on the right half
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Offset grid to the right side of the screen
                x = 1.0 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        """Helper to place mobjects on the defined A1-F6 grid."""
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        if grid_pos in self.grid:
            mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        # Implementation for Section 3: Understanding Binomial Distributions
        self.setup_layout(
            "Understanding Binomial Distributions", 
            [
                "- Fixed number of trials (n)",
                "- Success or Failure outcomes",
                "- Constant probability (p)",
                "- Independent trials"
            ]
        )
        
        # Represent the PMF formula
        formula = MathTex(
            "P(X=k) = \\binom{n}{k} p^k (1-p)^{n-k}",
            font_size=34,
            color="#00FFFF"
        )
        # Position using the grid system
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "C3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Visual indicator for success/failure (Binary outcome)
        success_dot = Dot(color="#00FF00", radius=0.2)
        failure_dot = Dot(color="#FF0000", radius=0.2)
        
        self.place_at_grid(success_dot, "E2")
        self.place_at_grid(failure_dot, "E4")
        
        success_label = Text("Success", font_size=20).next_to(success_dot, DOWN)
        failure_label = Text("Failure", font_size=20).next_to(failure_dot, DOWN)

        # Animations
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title))
        self.play(Create(self.lecture, run_time=2))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(Indicate(formula, color="#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(success_dot, shift=UP),
            FadeIn(failure_dot, shift=UP),
            Write(success_label),
            Write(failure_label)
        )
        
        # Highlight independent trials concept
        highlight_box = SurroundingRectangle(self.lecture[3], color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(highlight_box))
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(highlight_box), FadeOut(success_dot), FadeOut(failure_dot), FadeOut(success_label), FadeOut(failure_label))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Background and Title
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=32, color="#FFFFFF").to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = []
        for line in lecture_lines:
            t = Text(line, font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
            lecture_texts.append(t)
            
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5).shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        # Grid System for Right Side
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]
        
        # Centering the grid on the right half of the screen
        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Adjusting coordinates for the right side (x: 1 to 6, y: 2 to -3)
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.9
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.9
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup
        self.setup_layout(
            "Understanding Binomial Distributions",
            [
                "- n: Number of trials",
                "- p: Probability of success",
                "- k: Number of successes",
                "- Trials are independent",
                "- Formula: P(X=k) = (n choose k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k)"
            ]
        )
        
        self.play(Write(self.title))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture, shift=RIGHT))
        self.wait(1)

        # 2. Visualizing a Trial (Grid Interaction)
        # Success (Green)
        success_node = Circle(radius=0.35, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.8)
        success_label = Text("S", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF")
        success_grp = VGroup(success_node, success_label)
        
        # Failure (Red)
        failure_node = Circle(radius=0.35, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=0.8)
        failure_label = Text("F", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF")
        failure_grp = VGroup(failure_node, failure_label)

        # Place nodes on grid to demonstrate "n" trials
        trials = ["A1", "A2", "A3", "B1", "B2", "B3"]
        trial_outcomes = ["S", "F", "S", "S", "F", "S"]
        
        mobjects_to_show = []
        for pos, outcome in zip(trials, trial_outcomes):
            if outcome == "S":
                obj = success_grp.copy()
            else:
                obj = failure_grp.copy()
            self.place_at_grid(obj, pos)
            mobjects_to_show.append(obj)

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(m) for m in mobjects_to_show], lag_ratio=0.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Highlight Probability Formula
        formula = MathTex(
            "P(X=k) = \\binom{n}{k} p^k (1-p)^{n-k}",
            color="#FFFF00",
            font_size=36
        )
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "E3", scale_factor=1.2)
        # Shift slightly for better visibility
        formula.shift(RIGHT * 1.5)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(Indicate(formula, color="#FFFF00"))
        
        # 4. Final Scene Transition
        rect = Rectangle(color="#00FFFF", height=2.5, width=4.5)
        self.place_at_grid(rect, "D3")
        rect.shift(RIGHT * 1.5 + DOWN * 0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.wait(2)

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching current shared state info for consistency
        title_text = "Application and Summary"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Binomial distributions help us predict real-world outcomes.",
            "Quality control uses this to find defect probabilities.",
            "It's a powerful tool for repeated, independent trials."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for highlights and icons
        COLOR_LINE_1 = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_LINE_2 = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_LINE_3 = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_ROBOT = "#C0C0C0"
        COLOR_DEFECT = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_BOARD = "#2E7D32"  # Dark green for circuit board
        COLOR_TEXT = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # [self.wait(2.0)] Fade in Robot icon (#C0C0C0) and 100 circuit boards.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_LINE_1))
        self.wait(2.0)

        # Robot construction (using shapes for reliability if SVG not found)
        robot_head = Square(side_length=0.4, color=COLOR_ROBOT, fill_opacity=1)
        robot_body = Square(side_length=0.7, color=COLOR_ROBOT, fill_opacity=1).next_to(robot_head, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        robot_eye_l = Dot(radius=0.05, color=BLACK).move_to(robot_head.get_center() + LEFT*0.1)
        robot_eye_r = Dot(radius=0.05, color=BLACK).move_to(robot_head.get_center() + RIGHT*0.1)
        robot = VGroup(robot_head, robot_body, robot_eye_l, robot_eye_r)
        
        self.place_at_grid(robot, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)

        # 100 Circuit Boards (10x10 grid)
        boards = VGroup()
        for i in range(100):
            board = Rectangle(width=0.3, height=0.2, color=COLOR_BOARD, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=1)
            boards.add(board)
        
        boards.arrange_in_grid(rows=10, cols=10, buff=0.1)
        # Positioning the boards in a cluster on the right
        self.place_in_area(boards, "B3", "F6", scale_factor=0.7)

        self.play(FadeIn(robot), FadeIn(boards))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # [self.wait(1.5)] Highlight defective circuit boards in Red (#FF0000).
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_LINE_2))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # Selecting a few indices to represent defects (low probability)
        defect_indices = [12, 37, 58, 81]
        defects = VGroup(*[boards[i] for i in defect_indices])
        
        self.play(
            *[Indicate(board, color=COLOR_DEFECT) for board in defects],
            *[board.animate.set_fill(COLOR_DEFECT).set_color(COLOR_DEFECT) for board in defects]
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # [self.wait(2.0)] Fade out icons; show summary text in #FFFFFF.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_LINE_3))
        self.wait(2.0)

        # Fade out visual demo
        self.play(FadeOut(robot), FadeOut(boards))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Summary text
        summary_title = Text("Key Properties", font_size=26, color=COLOR_TEXT, weight=BOLD)
        summary_points = VGroup(
            Text("• Predicts outcomes in repeated trials", font_size=20, color=COLOR_TEXT),
            Text("• Assumes independence between trials", font_size=20, color=COLOR_TEXT),
            Text("• Constant probability of success (p)", font_size=20, color=COLOR_TEXT),
            Text("• Applicable to quality control & science", font_size=20, color=COLOR_TEXT)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.3)
        
        summary_vgroup = VGroup(summary_title, summary_points).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(summary_vgroup, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=0.9)

        self.play(FadeIn(summary_vgroup))
        self.wait(2.0)

outline.target_audience: High school or introductory college statistics students

sections.title: The Foundation: Bernoulli Trials
sections.content: Introduce prerequisite knowledge: The Bernoulli trial. Explain that a Binomial distribution is simply a series of these independent 'Yes/No' trials. Use a visual of a light switch (On/Off) or a coin toss.
sections.example: Meet 'Finn the Frog'. Every time Finn tries to catch a fly, he either succeeds (Success) or misses (Failure). If his success rate is always 70%, each single attempt is a Bernoulli trial.

sections.title: The BINS Criteria
sections.content: Define when a scenario qualifies as a Binomial Distribution using the BINS acronym: Binary (Success/Failure), Independent (one trial doesn't affect the next), Number (fixed number of trials 'n'), and Same probability 'p' for each trial. Use an animated checklist.
sections.example: Finn decides to catch exactly 10 flies (Fixed Number). Each jump is independent, the outcome is only caught or not caught (Binary), and his skill stays at 70% (Same 'p').

sections.title: The Mathematical Recipe (The Formula)
sections.content: Break down the formula P(X=k) = nCk * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Use color-coding to link the math to the visual: nCk (the number of ways to arrange successes), p^k (probability of successes), and (1-p)^(n-k) (probability of failures).
sections.example: To find the chance of Finn catching exactly 7 out of 10 flies, we calculate 10C7 (combinations of attempts) times 0.7 to the 7th power, times 0.3 to the 3rd power.

sections.title: Visualizing the Distribution
sections.content: Transition from a single calculation to a full probability histogram. Show how the shape changes based on 'p'. If p=0.5, it’s symmetric (like a bell curve); if p is high or low, the graph skews. Use an animated bar chart that 'grows' as we change the variables.
sections.example: A histogram showing the probability of Finn catching 0, 1, 2... up to 10 flies. Since his success is high (0.7), the tallest bars on the graph will cluster around 7.

sections.title: Application and Summary
sections.content: Summarize the key takeaways: Binomial distributions help us predict outcomes in repeated trials. Mention real-world applications like quality control in factories or pharmaceutical testing.
sections.example: A 'Quality Control Robot' checking a batch of 100 circuit boards for defects. If the defect rate is 2%, we use the Binomial distribution to predict the likelihood of finding more than 5 broken boards.

storyboard.title: The Foundation: Bernoulli Trials
lecture_lines: Bernoulli trials are the building blocks of binomial distributions.
Meet Finn. Every fly catch is a single trial.
Success means he catches the fly.
Failure means the fly escapes.
Finn's success rate stays constant at seventy percent.

storyboard.title: The BINS Criteria
lecture_lines: We use 'BINS' to check if a scenario fits.

Second, every trial must be Independent of others.

Finally, the probability 'p' must be the Same.

storyboard.title: The Mathematical Recipe (The Formula)
lecture_lines: The formula calculates the probability of exactly k successes.
'n choose k' counts the different ways to succeed.
'p' to the 'k' represents the successes' probability.
'1 minus p' to the 'n-k' represents failures.
Combine these parts to find the total probability.
